series_title: The Ancient World of Ice and Fire
episode_title: Before the Dragons: The Rise of Old Valyria
visual_cadence_rule: 30 images per minute (1 image every 2.0 seconds)
visual_qc_note: The fire batch, and the first time the narration has demanded flame — which reverses four batches of discipline. The five body-and-air frames keep the old rule (heat inside the animal) and the three fire frames that passed treat combustion as texture rather than as a light source. 0357 and 0358 are the best of them: the jet studied as a black-cored macro, and the aftermath carried entirely by melting stone with no body in frame. The batch's cost is entirely silhouette: 0355 collapsed the animal into a feathered fan at distance, and 0356 turned it into a bipedal fire demon.
four_limb_note: No limb-count failures this batch. Both rejections were silhouette legibility: a folded wing resolving as a ribbed fan at distance, and a reared neck with both wing-arms spread resolving as a bipedal figure. Limb number and silhouette legibility are separate checks and the second is now the harder one.
letterbox_scan_note: Per-row content-box scan run on every frame. 0356 and 0357 were full-bleed on arrival; 0351, 0352, 0353, 0354, 0357-pass-1 and 0358 carried strips (rows 12-755) and 0355 (rows 12-756); all cropped and resized back to 1376x768.
md5_verification_note: All seven uploaded frames were checked against local md5sum at upload time; the folder will be re-listed for a full pass once the batch completes.

scenes.visual_beat: Dynamic medium lateral tracking angle — Incandescent throat scutes & basalt-melting dragonfire
scenes.qc_note: APPROVED pass 1. Lateral tracking MS alongside the walking animal: basalt-black armour plates carried over muscle that rolls like something far lighter than stone — the verse's 'more supple than forged steel' rendered as carriage rather than as texture. Spine horizontal, body running out of frame at both ends so neither head nor tail closes the silhouette, hairline ember only in two plate seams. Reframed rows 12-755.

scenes.visual_beat: Compressed telephoto dramatic subject framing — Incandescent throat scutes & basalt-melting dragonfire
scenes.qc_note: APPROVED pass 1. 65mm compression of overlapping scutes stacking like hammered plate: thick opaque oxidised basalt-black faces, worn iron-grey edges where one overlaps the next, tight dark joins, irregular organic margins rather than machined edges. One ember hairline glowing deep in a seam. Armour filling the frame on all four sides, no head. Reframed rows 12-755.

scenes.visual_beat: Medium cinematic subject focus — Incandescent throat scutes & basalt-melting dragonfire
scenes.qc_note: APPROVED pass 1. Throat and chest at 50mm from below and to the side: scutes broader and thicker than bronze shields layered in descending rows, their edges worn to a dull bronze-grey from two centuries of use, with deep ember-red heat glowing between the rows from inside the flesh. Jaw and head out of frame above — no eye, no snout, no face. Reframed rows 12-755.

scenes.visual_beat: Wide environmental storytelling tableau — Incandescent throat scutes & basalt-melting dragonfire
scenes.qc_note: APPROVED pass 2. The animal at rest on a black shelf while damp mountain air turns to steam around it: sparse thin filaments of dull grey vapour peeling off the wet floor a few metres away and drifting upward, semi-transparent, never a cloud. Four limbs and a folded wing legible, thin ember cracks in the foreground rock, most of the frame dark. Pass 1 rendered the steam as a bright white fog machine filling the cave and had to be thrown out. Reframed rows 12-755.

scenes.visual_beat: High-elevation geographic / scale reveal — Incandescent throat scutes & basalt-melting dragonfire
scenes.qc_note: APPROVED pass 2. Ultra-wide from high on the wall looking steeply down: a cavern floor the size of a cathedral nave cracked into immense black basalt plates, the animal resting on it at about a fifth of the frame width and reading clearly as a four-legged beast with a long neck and tail and one folded wing lying flat as an unbroken sheet. Huge dark negative space, walls climbing out of frame. Pass 1 failed twice — the animal collapsed into a ribbed fan of plates and the floor came back flat mid-grey. Reframed rows 12-756.

scenes.visual_beat: Towering vertical scale composition — Incandescent throat scutes & basalt-melting dragonfire
scenes.qc_note: REJECTED. The throat glow and the compact orange-and-black jet from the jaws are both right, and the flame reads as pressurised rather than explosive. The failure is the animal: reared vertical with both wing-arms flung out symmetrically to left and right, the ember-lit chest filling the lower frame like a torso, so the whole frame resolves as a bipedal fire demon. This is the third bipedal failure in two batches. Rerender as PROFILE with the neck raised up and to the right, glow confined to throat and under-jaw, and the neck rising out of a heavy horizontal body held low across the bottom third with a forelimb and the folded wing on the floor.

scenes.visual_beat: Macro environmental / material texture insert — Incandescent throat scutes & basalt-melting dragonfire
scenes.qc_note: APPROVED pass 1. Macro of the flame at the moment it leaves the mouth: dense black core, translucent orange and amber outer layers, edges fraying into licks and black smoke, a few dull grey ash flecks drifting. Scorched jaw scutes at the frame edges are lit hot on their edges while their plate faces stay black. Studied as fire texture against stone, with no head and no eye. Full-bleed.

scenes.visual_beat: Intimate close-up detail / expression beat — Incandescent throat scutes & basalt-melting dragonfire
scenes.qc_note: APPROVED pass 1. Aftermath insert at 85mm: a patch of basalt ledge blistering and slumping where the flame has passed, its edge incandescent orange fading through dull red into black, vesicles catching their own glow, and a thin crust of matte grey ash lifting in flakes. The dark underside of the jaw sits out of focus beyond. Deliberately contains no body of any kind — the verse's 'flesh to ash' is carried by stone alone. Reframed rows 12-755.
